owner_requirements.title: recording takes
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.1, §21.3.** Arrangement recording creates take lanes and clips
on armed audio/MIDI tracks. Recording over existing clips adds a lane per pass,
including looping passes. Existing lanes are reused when no other clip exists
after the punch-in point. The latest recorded clip is copied to the main lane
and is available for playback. **U:** the reuse search order, first-pass
preexisting-main preservation and partial-pass clipping. The manual's reuse
condition does not establish a greedy lane-allocation algorithm.
owner_requirements.quote:
### REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-018 — recording takes

owner_requirements.title: lane visibility
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.1–21.2.** Audio/MIDI Arrangement tracks have a main lane and
can have multiple take lanes. Show Take Lanes toggles their visibility; inserting
a lane unfolds them. Take lanes are hidden in Automation Mode; requesting
their display or insertion exits that mode. **U:** display persistence and
accessibility/focus transitions beyond these actions.

accessibility/focus transitions beyond these actions.

owner_requirements.title: lane management
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.2.** Selected tracks accept Insert Take Lane. Lanes can be
duplicated, deleted, reordered within their track, renamed and resized.
Delete All Take Lanes removes all lanes; Delete All Unused Take Lanes removes
lanes lacking recorded material used in the main comp. **U:** sample-file
deletion, undo/redo grouping, linked tracks and edge conditions in unused-lane
classification. Deleting a lane is not evidence of deleting its audio file.
owner_requirements.quote:

classification. Deleting a lane is not evidence of deleting its audio file.

owner_requirements.title: audition
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.1, §21.5.** The main lane is normally heard; take lanes are
heard through Audition. The speaker control or T auditions a take lane. Only
one lane per track may be auditioned; different tracks may audition together.
When a selection spans lanes/tracks, the last selected lane per track is used.
**U:** audition/record overlap, switch timing, gaps, teardown and suppression of
the main lane during every audition boundary.

owner_requirements.title: comp copies and source independence
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.6.** Enter or Copy Selection to Main Lane copies selected take
material to the main lane. Main/take clips are independent copies: editing one
does not edit the other. This describes clip content independence, not a second
physical audio file. Take clips allow ordinary Arrangement edits and can be
copied/dragged to Session slots. **U:** cross-type paste refusal and exact
non-grid boundary handling.
owner_requirements.quote:

owner_requirements.title: choosing alternate comp material
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.6.** Ctrl on Windows/Cmd on macOS with Up/Down replaces selected
main material with previous/next take clips, skipping empty lanes. A take-lane
time selection also moves to the chosen take. Draw Mode copies a dragged take
selection to main on release; clicking a take with a main time selection
replaces the corresponding interval. **U:** dragging cancellation, endpoint
ties, cross-track selections and the no-alternative boundary.
owner_requirements.quote:

time selection also moves to the chosen take. Draw Mode copies a dragged take
selection to main on release; clicking a take with a main time selection
replaces the corresponding interval. **U:** dragging cancellation, endpoint
ties, cross-track selections and the no-alternative boundary.

owner_requirements.title: source highlights
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.7.** Used take material is highlighted with the track color;
unused material is desaturated. Highlights require matching clip positions and
properties. Dragging the highlight edge adjusts the split between adjacent
comp pieces. **U:** the complete property equivalence predicate, floating-point
tolerances and effects of unmatched edits. A shared TakeId alone does not prove
that two clips match.

owner_requirements.title: comp crossfades
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12, R21 §21.6.** With Create Fades on Clip Edges enabled, adjacent comp clips
receive four-millisecond crossfades. The documented manual crossfade command
also applies to selected clips. **U:** curve law, overlap/minimum-length rules,
rounding at sample rates and numerical render output. Four milliseconds is a
documented duration, not a measured waveform tolerance.
owner_requirements.quote:

rounding at sample rates and numerical render output. Four milliseconds is a
documented duration, not a measured waveform tolerance.

owner_requirements.title: stored lane inventory
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12403, E-SCHEMA; E-DOCS.** Both AudioTrack and MidiTrack declare TakeLanes.
Its nested TakeLanes list holds TakeLane entries and a folded-state field.
TakeLane declares name, annotation, height, selection, clip automation and
Audition fields, with `ClipAutomation/Events` holding saved clips. AudioClip and
MidiClip declare TakeId. Shipped documents corroborate concrete lane entries
and MIDI clips. This requirement inventories stored state; it does not assert
allocation, source matching, numeric range, save/restore behavior or how TakeId
is generated. Existing document specs govern common field parsing.

owner_requirements.title: save, undo, redo and deletion lifecycle
owner_requirements.contract:
**U.** Other than the documented Undo clauses in REQ-006, 009 and 011, no
recording/comp transaction boundary or redo result is established. Persistence
of an in-progress record, captured history, audition state, lane fold/selection,
comp linkage, unsaved recordings and physical sample ownership remains open.
Schema declarations cannot settle these behaviors. No recovery guarantee follows
from the presence of a saved clip.
owner_requirements.quote:
### REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-028 — save, undo, redo and deletion lifecycle

of an in-progress record, captured history, audition state, lane fold/selection,
comp linkage, unsaved recordings and physical sample ownership remains open.
Schema declarations cannot settle these behaviors. No recovery guarantee follows
from the presence of a saved clip.

owner_requirements.title: cancellation, failure and teardown
owner_requirements.contract:
**U.** Stop is a documented recording/clip control (REQ-007, 031), but cancel
before start, stop during count-in, disconnecting an input, disk full, permission
failure, sample-write failure, device/track deletion, closing the Set while
recording and process failure have no established transition or error wording.
Retained media, final note-offs, retry and rollback results must remain ungraded.
owner_requirements.quote:
### REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-029 — cancellation, failure and teardown

**U.** Stop is a documented recording/clip control (REQ-007, 031), but cancel
before start, stop during count-in, disconnecting an input, disk full, permission
failure, sample-write failure, device/track deletion, closing the Set while
recording and process failure have no established transition or error wording.
Retained media, final note-offs, retry and rollback results must remain ungraded.

owner_requirements.title: recording timing
owner_requirements.contract:
**U.** No bound is established for input-to-note/sample timestamp, monitor or
record latency compensation, buffer scheduling, punch inclusivity, click-free
switching, jitter or real-time capacity. The monitoring-latency preference
documented by R17 §17.1 has no numeric transfer rule here. Clip-launch and
playback-core timing results cannot be substituted for the recording path.
owner_requirements.quote:
### REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-030 — recording timing

**U.** No bound is established for input-to-note/sample timestamp, monitor or

blocks.text: 21. Comping
blocks.raw_html: 21. Comping

blocks.text: Comping makes it possible to pick the best moments of each recorded performance and combine them into a composite track (also known as a “comp”). Live can create take lanes in a track as you record material, which you can use to piece your favorite parts together. You can also store alternative versions of a clip arrangement on multiple take lanes, or drag samples from your library onto take lanes and use comping as a creative sample-chopping tool.
blocks.raw_html: Comping makes it possible to pick the best moments of each recorded performance and combine them into a composite track (also known as a “comp”). Live can create take lanes in a track as you record material, which you can use to piece your favorite parts together. You can also store alternative versions of a clip arrangement on multiple take lanes, or drag samples from your library onto take lanes and use comping as a creative sample-chopping tool.

blocks.text: 21.1 Take Lanes
blocks.raw_html: 21.1 Take Lanes

blocks.text: Every audio or MIDI track in the Arrangement View can consist of multiple parallel lanes. The first lane of a track is the main lane, which is audible by default. A track can also have any number of take lanes, which are only audible when Audition Mode is enabled.
blocks.raw_html: Every audio or MIDI track in the Arrangement View can consist of multiple parallel lanes. The first lane of a track is the main lane, which is audible by default. A track can also have any number of take lanes, which are only audible when Audition Mode is enabled.

blocks.text: Take lanes are automatically created when recording new clips in the Arrangement and can also be inserted manually.
blocks.raw_html: Take lanes are automatically created when recording new clips in the Arrangement and can also be inserted manually.

blocks.text: You can toggle the visibility of take lanes by choosing the Show Take Lanes command from a track header’s context menu, or by using the Show/Hide Take Lanes toggle in a track’s main lane.
blocks.raw_html: You can toggle the visibility of take lanes by choosing the Show Take Lanes command from a track header’s context menu, or by using the Show/Hide Take Lanes toggle in a track’s main lane.

blocks.text: The shortcut for showing or hiding take lanes is CtrlAltU (Win) / CmdOptionU (Mac).
blocks.raw_html: The shortcut for showing or hiding take lanes is CtrlAltU (Win) / CmdOptionU (Mac).

blocks.text: You can use the left arrow key to navigate from a take lane to the main lane. This also folds all take lanes.
blocks.raw_html: You can use the left arrow key to navigate from a take lane to the main lane. This also folds all take lanes.

blocks.text: Note that take lanes are not shown when Automation Mode is enabled. You can still access the Show Take Lanes command and insert take lanes while in Automation Mode, but either action exits the mode to show all take lanes.
blocks.raw_html: Note that take lanes are not shown when Automation Mode is enabled. You can still access the Show Take Lanes command and insert take lanes while in Automation Mode, but either action exits the mode to show all take lanes.

blocks.text: 21.2 Inserting and Managing Take Lanes
blocks.raw_html: 21.2 Inserting and Managing Take Lanes

blocks.text: You can manually insert a take lane into one or multiple selected tracks by choosing the Insert Take Lane command from the Create menu. The same command can be used from a track or take lane header’s context menu or via the shortcut ShiftAltT (Win) / ShiftOptionT (Mac). Inserting a take lane also unfolds any existing lanes if they are not already visible.
blocks.raw_html: You can manually insert a take lane into one or multiple selected tracks by choosing the Insert Take Lane command from the Create menu. The same command can be used from a track or take lane header’s context menu or via the shortcut ShiftAltT (Win) / ShiftOptionT (Mac). Inserting a take lane also unfolds any existing lanes if they are not already visible.

blocks.text: Note that you can also create take lanes and add clips to existing ones via the Live API with Max for Live.
blocks.raw_html: Note that you can also create take lanes and add clips to existing ones via the Live API with Max for Live.

blocks.text: Take lanes can be duplicated with the CtrlD (Win) / CmdD (Mac) shortcut, or via the Duplicate command in a take lane header’s context menu.
blocks.raw_html: Take lanes can be duplicated with the CtrlD (Win) / CmdD (Mac) shortcut, or via the Duplicate command in a take lane header’s context menu.

blocks.text: You can delete take lanes with the Backspace or Delete key, or via the Delete command in the Edit menu.
blocks.raw_html: You can delete take lanes with the Backspace or Delete key, or via the Delete command in the Edit menu.

blocks.text: To remove all take lanes from a track, use the Delete All Take Lanes command in a track or take lane header’s context menu. The Delete All Unused Take Lanes command removes any take lanes that do not contain recorded material within a comp on the track’s main lane.
blocks.raw_html: To remove all take lanes from a track, use the Delete All Take Lanes command in a track or take lane header’s context menu. The Delete All Unused Take Lanes command removes any take lanes that do not contain recorded material within a comp on the track’s main lane.

blocks.text: You can resize take lanes vertically by pressing Alt+ (Win) / Option+ (Mac) or Alt- (Win) / Option- (Mac), or by holding Alt (Win) / Option (Mac) and using the mouse wheel. These shortcuts resize all selected take lanes simultaneously.
blocks.raw_html: You can resize take lanes vertically by pressing Alt+ (Win) / Option+ (Mac) or Alt- (Win) / Option- (Mac), or by holding Alt (Win) / Option (Mac) and using the mouse wheel. These shortcuts resize all selected take lanes simultaneously.

blocks.text: The resize handles that appear when hovering over the edge of a take lane can also be used to adjust the height of one or multiple selected lanes.
blocks.raw_html: The resize handles that appear when hovering over the edge of a take lane can also be used to adjust the height of one or multiple selected lanes.

blocks.text: You can reorder take lanes within their track by dragging and dropping them, or by holding the Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) modifier and pressing the up or down arrow key.
blocks.raw_html: You can reorder take lanes within their track by dragging and dropping them, or by holding the Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) modifier and pressing the up or down arrow key.

blocks.text: To rename take lanes, use the Rename command in the Edit menu or a take lane header’s context menu. The keyboard shortcut is CtrlR (Win) / CmdR (Mac). Multiple take lanes can be renamed simultaneously. Use the Tab and ShiftTab shortcuts to move between lanes and tracks while renaming them.
blocks.raw_html: To rename take lanes, use the Rename command in the Edit menu or a take lane header’s context menu. The keyboard shortcut is CtrlR (Win) / CmdR (Mac). Multiple take lanes can be renamed simultaneously. Use the Tab and ShiftTab shortcuts to move between lanes and tracks while renaming them.

blocks.text: 21.3 Recording Takes
blocks.raw_html: 21.3 Recording Takes

blocks.text: While recording new clips in the Arrangement View, take lanes are automatically added to armed audio and MIDI tracks, and clips are created within those take lanes.
blocks.raw_html: While recording new clips in the Arrangement View, take lanes are automatically added to armed audio and MIDI tracks, and clips are created within those take lanes.

blocks.text: Recording over existing clips, either by recording individual passes or by recording in a loop, adds a new take lane for each pass. Existing take lanes are automatically reused when no other clip exists after the punch-in point.
blocks.raw_html: Recording over existing clips, either by recording individual passes or by recording in a loop, adds a new take lane for each pass. Existing take lanes are automatically reused when no other clip exists after the punch-in point.

blocks.text: The last recorded clip in a track is always copied to that track’s main lane so that it becomes immediately audible when playing back the Set.
blocks.raw_html: The last recorded clip in a track is always copied to that track’s main lane so that it becomes immediately audible when playing back the Set.

blocks.text: Note that recorded clips inherit their track’s color by default. You can configure Live to automatically assign a different color to each take by setting the Clip Color toggle to Random in the Theme & Colors Settings.
blocks.raw_html: Note that recorded clips inherit their track’s color by default. You can configure Live to automatically assign a different color to each take by setting the Clip Color toggle to Random in the Theme & Colors Settings.

blocks.text: 21.4 Inserting Samples
blocks.raw_html: 21.4 Inserting Samples

blocks.text: You can drag samples and MIDI files to take lanes from the browser or File Explorer/Finder. When multiple samples are selected, hold the Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) modifier key while dragging to insert each sample into sequential tracks.
blocks.raw_html: You can drag samples and MIDI files to take lanes from the browser or File Explorer/Finder. When multiple samples are selected, hold the Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) modifier key while dragging to insert each sample into sequential tracks.

blocks.text: 21.5 Auditioning Take Lanes
blocks.raw_html: 21.5 Auditioning Take Lanes

blocks.text: You can audition a take lane by clicking the Audition Take Lane button (displayed as a speaker icon) in that take lane’s header, or using the T keyboard shortcut.
blocks.raw_html: You can audition a take lane by clicking the Audition Take Lane button (displayed as a speaker icon) in that take lane’s header, or using the T keyboard shortcut.

blocks.text: Note that while you can audition take lanes from different tracks at the same time, you can only audition one take lane per track. If a time selection or lane header selection includes multiple take lanes from different tracks, the last selected lane for each track is auditioned.
blocks.raw_html: Note that while you can audition take lanes from different tracks at the same time, you can only audition one take lane per track. If a time selection or lane header selection includes multiple take lanes from different tracks, the last selected lane for each track is auditioned.

blocks.text: 21.6 Creating a Comp
blocks.raw_html: 21.6 Creating a Comp

blocks.text: Selected material in take lanes can be copied to the main lane by pressing the Enter key or via a take lane’s Copy Selection to Main Lane context menu command.
blocks.raw_html: Selected material in take lanes can be copied to the main lane by pressing the Enter key or via a take lane’s Copy Selection to Main Lane context menu command.

blocks.text: It is possible to replace clips in a track’s main lane with the next or previous take lane clips by selecting clip headers or making a time selection within the main lane or a take lane and then holding Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) while pressing the up or down arrow key. If the time selection is on a take lane, the selection also moves to the next or previous take. Note that empty take lanes are ignored.
blocks.raw_html: It is possible to replace clips in a track’s main lane with the next or previous take lane clips by selecting clip headers or making a time selection within the main lane or a take lane and then holding Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) while pressing the up or down arrow key. If the time selection is on a take lane, the selection also moves to the next or previous take. Note that empty take lanes are ignored.

blocks.text: In Draw Mode, selected take lane material can be copied to a track’s main lane in one single gesture by clicking, dragging, and then releasing the mouse. It is also possible to replace the clips in a time selection on the main lane by clicking on a take lane to insert the corresponding portion of that take into the selection.
blocks.raw_html: In Draw Mode, selected take lane material can be copied to a track’s main lane in one single gesture by clicking, dragging, and then releasing the mouse. It is also possible to replace the clips in a time selection on the main lane by clicking on a take lane to insert the corresponding portion of that take into the selection.

blocks.text: The clips added to a track’s main lane are independent copies of the corresponding take lane clips. This means that you can freely edit clips in the main lane without modifying the original take lane clips and vice versa. Clips in take lanes can be edited the same way as other clips in the Arrangement View: they can be moved, copied/pasted, dragged/dropped, consolidated, cropped, or duplicated. Take lane clips can also be moved to Session View clip slots by either copying and pasting or dragging and dropping.

blocks.text: You can prevent clicks between clips by enabling the Create Fades on Clip Edges option in the Record, Warp & Launch Settings. When enabled, four-millisecond crossfades are automatically created for adjacent clips. You can also manually create these crossfades by selecting multiple clips and pressing CtrlAltF (Win) / CmdOptionF (Mac).

blocks.text: 21.7 Source Highlights
blocks.raw_html: 21.7 Source Highlights

blocks.text: For every comp in a main lane, the source material in the corresponding take lanes is highlighted in the track’s color. All unused take lane material is displayed in a desaturated shade of the track’s color. This makes it easier to identify which recorded material is part of the comp. Note that source highlights will only be shown when the clips have matching positions and properties.

Note that source highlights will only be shown when the clips have matching positions and properties.

blocks.text: Source highlights on take lanes can be resized to adjust the split point between two adjacent parts of a comp by dragging the edge of the highlight.

proposals.title: Visibility/navigation and Automation Mode entry branches
proposals.proposed_action: In separate editable Arrangement copies with admitted take lanes, actually invoke the track-header Show Take Lanes context command, the main-lane Show/Hide toggle and the exact offered CtrlAltU(Win)/CmdOptionU(Mac) shortcut in show/hide histories. From an actually selected take lane press Left Arrow and observe main-lane selection/folding. In separately reset Automation Mode histories actually invoke Show and then Insert Take Lane, recording mode/visible lanes; RC045 already does Show, not Insert.
proposals.positive_baseline: UI-only accepted selected take/main context, existing lanes and actual initial visibility/Automation Mode recorded; no audio/hardware required. Before any output/loss observation establish independently productive main and take histories.
proposals.limits: No keyboard focus/OS alias/accessibility/persistence/default or exact fold-animation timing law; left-arrow behavior not arbitrary from every focus.

proposals.title: Lane insert/duplicate/delete actual entry alternatives
proposals.proposed_action: Use disposable copies with known lane/clip identities. Actually insert into one then two selected tracks via separately reset Create menu, track-header context, lane-header context and exact offered ShiftAltT(Win)/ShiftOptionT(Mac). Actually duplicate via header Duplicate and CtrlD/CmdD; delete separately via offered Backspace/Delete and Edit Delete. Independently invoke Delete All Take Lanes, retaining true RC048 Delete All Unused as a separate operation with recorded used/unused material.
proposals.positive_baseline: Known existing editable lane and successful duplicate/insertion before deletion/absence; independently known recorded used and unused source material and genuine main comp before unused classification. UI actions need no audio; audio-loss trials require each take/main actually productive first.
proposals.limits: No physical sample-file deletion, undo grouping, complete unused predicate, cross-track delete/frozen behavior or arbitrary path acceptance; unavailable route stays U.

proposals.title: Resize entry gestures and selected-lane scope
proposals.proposed_action: On one then multiple selected take lanes actually use the offered Alt+(Win)/Option+(Mac), Alt-(Win)/Option-(Mac), modifier+wheel and hover-edge resize handles in separate reset histories. Record selected versus nonselected lane identity/visible height before and after.
proposals.positive_baseline: UI-only admitted editable lane edges and independently offered input route; establish a visible positive size change before a subsequent reset/no-change contrast. No audio/hardware requirement.
proposals.limits: No height pixel/step/minimum/maximum, OS event code, default, persistence or unselected-effect law beyond source selected scope.

proposals.title: Reorder and rename routes/multiselection traversal
proposals.proposed_action: Within one track with distinguishable lanes actually reorder via drag/drop then separately Ctrl/Cmd Up and Down. Actually invoke Edit Rename, header-context Rename and CtrlR/CmdR on reset selected lanes; then separately rename multiple selected lanes and use Tab/ShiftTab while renaming across admitted lanes/tracks. Preserve RC047 category actions.
proposals.positive_baseline: UI-only known lane identities/order and admitted editable names/selection; establish productive reorder/rename once before a no-effect query. No audio required.
proposals.limits: No cross-track reorder, name grammar/uniqueness, exact focus wrap, OS alias, undo/restore or numeric resize law.

proposals.title: Productive recording-take and reuse-history prerequisites
proposals.proposed_action: Retain RC043 complete audio/MIDI over-record passes and RC044 no-clip-after-punch-in reuse. Refine future histories with a separately admitted first-empty-track capture, independently identifiable successive full takes, and actual main playback of the last recorded clip. Record offered lane/clip identities without selecting an allocation order.
proposals.positive_baseline: Each armed eligible track has independently admitted active owned input, accepted recording trigger and genuinely NONEMPTY completed take with NONZERO nonmuted playback. BOTH distinct takes and main comp independently productive before reuse/loss/order comparisons; flags alone cannot supply takes.
proposals.limits: R-G04 partial passes, reuse search order, first-main preservation and R-G05–09 undo/media/restore/cancel/crossfade remain U. No immediate-output deadline or new duplicate recording case adopted.

proposals.title: Actual library/file-to-take insertion and multiple-sample track destination
proposals.proposed_action: On admitted audio/MIDI tracks actually drag one owned supported sample and one admitted MIDI file to a take lane from Browser, then separately from platform Explorer/Finder. With multiple known samples selected, hold Ctrl(Win)/Cmd(Mac) while dragging and record the sequential TRACK destinations, not sequential take lanes.
proposals.positive_baseline: Known valid owned NONEMPTY files, admitted drop targets and genuine successful loaded clip/output history before replacement/cancel/absence. MIDI/audio admission separate; actual output requires independently productive instrument/route/nonzero gain. UI-only location observations need no audio.
proposals.limits: No decoder/format grammar/universal admission, multi-MIDI distribution, sample ordering, transaction/cancel or file-copy law; source creative suggestion does not guarantee a preferred sound.

Retain true RC049 same-track switching and RC050 different-track simultaneous audition. In separate histories form a time selection then a lane-header selection spanning multiple take lanes on DIFFERENT tracks, with recorded selection order; invoke audition and inspect last selected lane per track.
proposals.positive_baseline: BOTH distinct identifiable takes on each tested track AND its main comp independently have genuine NONEMPTY NONZERO nonmuted productive output before switching/loss; each track productive separately before simultaneous audition. UI-only button/selection checks need no audio.
proposals.limits: No constructor/default reset, universal main-suppression-at-boundaries, switch latency, gap/tail/no-click, note codec or all-stopped output law; unavailable T focus remains U.

proposals.limits: No no-alternative wrap/tie rule, sample/grid rounding, cross-track substitution or physical second file; RC054 BOTH Draw-release/main-click actions and RC076 cancellation U remain unchanged.

proposals.limits: Existing Arrangement/Session/clip owners retain edit, launch and file laws; no all-edit completion, exact move/copy ownership transaction or duplication of physical media inferred.
